glyhub

glyhub collects glycomics and glycoproteomics data for the Glycoverse ecosystem, using the GlycomicSE and GlycoproteomicSE containers from glyexp. The package is experimental.

Available data

34 datasets from 17 public GlycoPOST projects are bundled, including released glycans, glycosaminoglycan disaccharides and site/charge-resolved glycopeptides. Objects combine source-defined quantitative tables from the same study and glycan class where measurement definitions are compatible. GPST000602 is explicitly an annotated-peak subset with spectrum-specific, unaligned feature identities. Inclusion does not imply recovery of every experiment in its paper.

Each dataset has its own help page describing the biological system, experimental design, units, source table and limitations. Use data(package = "glyhub") for the installed catalog. N/O classes remain separate; source experiments, sample conditions and replicate labels remain in colData. Feature unions use documented author keys or supported structures, with an explicit source-coverage mask for unmeasured combinations. The two GPST000738 enzyme assays remain separate because their normalization reference sets differ. GPST000578 retains three measurement groups because total peak area, source repeatability intensity and inter-instrument peak area cannot be assumed to have identical measurement definitions. Former names are listed in the migration map.

Zero-valued abundances are stored as NA in the distributed assays. Original values, source-missing values and conflict masks remain in metadata. No imputation or renormalization is applied. Unknown molecular annotations remain NA without removing quantitative rows, except for the documented annotated-only peak subset in GPST000602; its excluded source rows remain in the provenance ledger. Structures are encoded only from explicit source structural evidence; unresolved bonds and attachment positions remain uncertain.

Notable limits include source-column conflicts in GPST000213, source annotation conflicts in GPST000035, and uncertain positional assignments in several datasets. Charge-state features in GPST000533 are not independent biological replicates. Original source licenses and repository terms are recorded separately from the package’s code license. See the curation audit, 20-project review, and object inventory.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("glycoverse/glyhub")

Example 

x <- glyhub::glyhub_GPST000738_N_B4GalT1
dim(x)
#> [1]  9 18
data.frame(as.list(S4Vectors::metadata(x)$processing_counts))
#>   source_missing source_nd conflict zero_to_na
#> 1              0         0       24          6

Data use R’s LazyData mechanism. SummarizedExperiment::assay(x) contains the curated abundance matrix; S4Vectors::metadata(x)$raw_abundance preserves the unconverted values. rowData(x) retains typed glyrepr annotations and source evidence, and colData(x) retains source conditions and observation locations.

Reproduction

Original inputs and scripts are grouped by accession under data-raw/GPST000643/ and data-raw/GPST000738/. From the package root:

source("data-raw/build.R")
# Check that rebuilding preserves scientific contents:
source("data-raw/validate-reproduction.R")

See validation results. See ?glyhub_data_conventions for shared measurement and annotation conventions.
